questions.text: A derivative is a financial instrument whose value is derived from:
options: An underlying asset such as a stock, bond, commodity or index
questions.explanation: A derivative’s price depends on the value or performance of an underlying asset such as equity, bond, commodity, currency or index.

questions.text: A liquidity ratio of 6 indicates that:
options: Liquid assets can cover 6 months of expenses
questions.explanation: It means the person can survive 6 months without new income.

questions.text: Redemption proceeds of NRI investments made on a non-repatriable basis are credited to:
questions.explanation: Non-repatriable proceeds are credited to the NRO account of the NRI investor.

questions.text: A 'risk-averse' investor will:
options: Always choose the highest return regardless of risk
Prefer investments with lower risk for a given return
Ignore the level of risk while investing
questions.explanation: Risk-averse investors prefer lower risk for a given return and demand a risk premium for taking additional risk.

questions.text: Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) issued by depositories includes:
options: Holdings across mutual funds and demat securities linked to PAN
questions.explanation: CAS provides a consolidated view of all mutual fund and demat holdings linked to an investor’s PAN.

questions.text: Which department of the Ministry of Finance deals with public sector banks, insurance, and pension reforms?
options: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
questions.explanation: The Department of Financial Services administers policies on public sector banks, insurance and pension reforms.

questions.text: Why should cash-flow statements be reviewed periodically?
options: Income and expenses remain constant always
To identify changes in income, expenses or new commitments early
questions.explanation: Regular review keeps the plan aligned with life changes and goals.

questions.text: A callable bond is one where:
options: The investor can redeem early at a predetermined price
The issuer has the right to redeem the bond before maturity
The coupon rate changes automatically with inflation
The bond has no maturity date
questions.explanation: Callable bonds give the issuer the right to redeem the bond prematurely, usually when interest rates fall, increasing reinvestment risk for investors.

questions.text: AIFs must issue to investors:
options: A Key Information Memorandum similar to mutual funds
questions.explanation: AIFs raise funds through private placement by issuing a detailed Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) to investors.

questions.text: The Rule of 72 gives:
options: Exact number of years to double an amount
Approximate years to double money at given rate
Half of the rate of return
questions.explanation: Rule of 72 approximates doubling time = 72 ÷ rate of return.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about asset allocation is TRUE?
options: It has minimal impact on portfolio performance
It is the key determinant of long-term portfolio returns and risk
It focuses only on stock selection
It can be ignored once the portfolio is constructed
questions.explanation: Empirical studies show asset allocation is the major driver of a portfolio’s long-term risk and return.

questions.text: Under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, a mutual fund is constituted as:
questions.explanation: Every mutual fund is set up as a trust under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, with the sponsor, trustees, and AMC as constituents.

questions.text: Which of the following powers does SEBI NOT possess?
options: Criminal prosecution authority in regular courts
questions.explanation: SEBI has quasi-legislative, executive, and judicial powers but cannot directly prosecute criminal cases—it refers them to courts.

questions.text: If ₹5,000 is invested monthly in an SIP earning 10% p.a., compounded monthly, for 10 years, the total corpus (approx.) will be:
questions.explanation: Using FV of annuity formula, FV ≈ 5,000×((1+0.00833)¹²⁰−1)/0.00833 ≈ 10.3 lakh.

questions.text: If an investor remains unsatisfied after SCORES closure, the next escalation is to:
options: Ombudsman or Arbitration mechanism at exchange or SEBI-recognized body
questions.explanation: Investors may approach SEBI’s Ombudsman or exchange arbitration for unresolved cases.

questions.text: Circuit filters or price bands are imposed to:
options: Prevent extreme price movements in a single day
questions.explanation: Circuit filters cap daily price moves within a band to curb excessive volatility.

questions.text: The Registrar of Companies (RoC) is responsible for:
options: Registering companies and monitoring compliance with company law
questions.explanation: RoC registers companies and ensures they comply with provisions of the Companies Act.

questions.text: High DTI ratio implies:
questions.explanation: A large part of income is tied to EMIs, reducing flexibility.

questions.text: Setting exposure limits to sectors and asset classes helps to:
questions.explanation: Exposure limits prevent excessive concentration in a single sector or security, reducing portfolio risk.

questions.text: For mutual fund investors, the first point of contact for grievances is:
options: The concerned AMC or its Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA)
questions.explanation: Investors should first approach the AMC or its RTA; unresolved issues can then be escalated to SEBI through SCORES.

questions.text: Diversification helps primarily to reduce:
questions.explanation: Diversification reduces company-specific (unsystematic) risk but not market-wide (systematic) risk.

questions.text: The minimum investment amount a client must place with a Portfolio Manager is:
questions.explanation: SEBI regulations stipulate a minimum investment of ₹50 lakh for investors availing PMS.

questions.text: In the corporate bond market, trades are typically settled through:
questions.explanation: Corporate bonds are traded and settled through exchanges and their clearing corporations.

questions.text: An ethical response, if a mistake is made in executing client instructions, is to:
options: Hide the error and hope markets recover
Promptly disclose the error, correct it, and compensate where required
questions.explanation: Honesty and accountability require disclosure of mistakes, corrective action, and fair compensation if client suffers loss.

questions.text: A positive Jensen’s Alpha indicates:
options: Portfolio outperformed relative to its systematic risk
questions.explanation: A positive alpha means the portfolio delivered higher return than expected for its risk level, indicating superior management.

questions.text: Government bonds compared to corporate bonds are generally considered to have:
options: Higher credit risk and higher yield
Lower credit risk and often lower yield
No market price fluctuation risk at all
questions.explanation: Sovereign bonds usually have lower credit risk, so they tend to offer lower yields compared to corporate bonds of similar maturity.

questions.text: The efficient frontier represents:
options: The set of portfolios with the highest return for a given level of risk
The set of portfolios with the lowest return and highest risk
All possible combinations of risky and risk-free assets
questions.explanation: The efficient frontier shows the optimal portfolios that provide maximum expected return for a given risk or minimum risk for a given return.

questions.text: A client wanting to retire early at age 50 instead of 60 will generally need to:
options: Save more and invest more aggressively in earlier years
questions.explanation: Early retirement means fewer earning years and more retired years, requiring higher saving and often more growth-oriented investments.

questions.text: Correlation between two asset classes helps to:
questions.explanation: Lower correlation among asset classes provides diversification benefits and reduces portfolio risk.

questions.text: The buyer of a call option has the:
options: Obligation to buy the underlying asset
Right but not the obligation to buy the underlying asset
Obligation to sell the underlying asset
Right to receive fixed interest payments
questions.explanation: A call option gives its holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy the underlying asset at a predetermined price within a period.

questions.text: In case of transmission without nomination, the claimant must provide:
questions.explanation: For non-nominated cases, claimant must provide a death certificate, legal heir certificate, or notarized will copy.

questions.text: Equity shares represent:
options: An ownership interest in the company
A fixed-income investment with guaranteed return
questions.explanation: Equity shares signify ownership in the company and entitle the holder to dividends and voting rights.

questions.text: Flat-rate interest means:
options: Interest charged only on reducing principal
Interest calculated on full principal throughout the term
questions.explanation: Flat-rate computes interest on entire loan amount for full tenure, overstating true cost.

questions.text: Why is it important to prioritise financial goals?
options: Because only one goal can be achieved
Because resources are usually limited and not all goals can be met simultaneously
To avoid investing in equity products
questions.explanation: Most people face resource constraints, so goals must be ranked to allocate savings effectively.

questions.text: Which factor MOST strongly supports higher equity exposure in a client’s portfolio?
options: Short time horizon and low risk tolerance
Long time horizon and high risk tolerance
questions.explanation: Equities suit investors with long horizons and higher risk appetite.

questions.text: A stock split means:
options: Company merges two shares into one
Company divides each share into smaller units to increase liquidity
Company issues new shares for cash
questions.explanation: A stock split divides shares into smaller units to make them more affordable and increase liquidity.

questions.text: Which of the following asset classes generally has the highest short-term price volatility?
questions.explanation: Equities are typically the most volatile in the short term compared to the other options listed.

questions.text: Net Asset Value (NAV) per unit is calculated as:
options: Net assets divided by face value
Number of units divided by net assets
Net assets divided by number of outstanding units
Total investments divided by number of investors
questions.explanation: NAV per unit = Net assets / Number of outstanding units.

questions.text: A family has monthly income ₹1,50,000, total expenses ₹1,35,000 including ₹30,000 discretionary. What is the discretionary expense ratio?
questions.explanation: 30,000 ÷ 1,50,000 = 20% actually? Wait check: 30/150 = 0.2 = 20%; adjust to 20% (index 1).

questions.text: In a conservative hybrid fund, the typical allocation to debt and equity is:
questions.explanation: Conservative hybrid funds predominantly invest in debt (75–90%) with a small equity allocation of 10–25%.

questions.text: Which of the following participants typically use derivatives to hedge?
options: Producers or investors exposed to price or rate risk
questions.explanation: Hedgers use derivatives to protect themselves against adverse movements in prices or interest rates.

questions.text: Risk capacity in financial planning refers to:
options: Client’s financial ability to absorb losses without derailing goals
questions.explanation: Risk capacity is the financial ability to take risk, based on income, assets, liabilities and time horizon.

questions.text: A puttable bond:
options: Allows the issuer to repay early at a lower price
Allows the investor to sell the bond back to the issuer at a pre-specified price on certain dates
questions.explanation: Puttable bonds give bondholders the right to sell the bond back to the issuer at a pre-set price, reducing interest rate risk for investors.

questions.text: Inflation risk for a fixed rate bond investor is:
options: Risk that inflation will fall and real returns rise
Risk that higher inflation erodes the real purchasing power of fixed coupon and principal
Risk that bond cannot be redeemed at par
Risk that bond will be converted into equity
questions.explanation: If inflation rises, the real (inflation-adjusted) value of fixed coupons and principal declines, which is inflation risk.

questions.text: Under SEBI regulations, intermediaries must retain records for a minimum period of:
questions.explanation: SEBI requires intermediaries to maintain client and transaction records for at least five years.

questions.text: Equity is generally RECOMMENDED as part of a client’s portfolio because:
options: It enhances long-term growth potential despite short-term volatility
questions.explanation: Equity contributes to long-term growth in a diversified portfolio, though it carries higher short-term risk.

questions.text: Net assets of a mutual fund scheme are defined as:
options: Face value of units multiplied by number of units
Total assets minus total liabilities and expenses of the scheme
Total market value of securities only
Total cash balance in bank accounts
questions.explanation: Net assets are arrived at by taking the current value of the portfolio plus current assets and subtracting expenses and liabilities of the scheme.

questions.text: Who publishes daily reference rates for major currency pairs like USD/INR?
questions.explanation: FBIL publishes daily reference rates for key currency pairs on Mumbai business days.

questions.text: Transmission of mutual fund units occurs when:
options: Investor wants to transfer to a friend
Investor dies and legal heir claims ownership
questions.explanation: Transmission refers to the transfer of ownership of mutual fund units to legal heirs or nominees upon death of the holder.

questions.text: Psychographic analysis of an investor helps in:
options: Understanding behavioural traits and risk personality
questions.explanation: Psychographic analysis identifies behavioural and personality characteristics affecting investment decisions and risk profile.

questions.text: Defaulting on EMI payments generally leads to:
options: Penalty charges and lower credit rating
questions.explanation: Non-payment attracts penalties and adversely impacts credit record.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of a Portfolio Manager?
options: Maintaining client funds in a separate bank account
Investing unlimited amounts in associate companies
questions.explanation: A Portfolio Manager cannot invest more than 30% of client assets in associate or related entities, and must act in fiduciary capacity.

questions.text: If a complaint remains unresolved even after arbitration, an investor may approach:
questions.explanation: Investors can approach Consumer Courts or High Courts if dissatisfied after arbitration.

questions.text: The minimum corpus for each AIF scheme must be at least:
questions.explanation: Each AIF scheme must have a minimum corpus of ₹50 crore, while angel funds have relaxed limits.

questions.text: Non-discretionary Portfolio Managers:
options: Require client approval for every transaction
Can invest only in government securities
questions.explanation: Non-discretionary Portfolio Managers act based on the client’s instructions for every investment decision.

questions.text: In a multi-cap fund, SEBI requires that at least 75% of assets are in equity with minimum allocation of:
options: 25% in large-cap, 25% in mid-cap, 25% in small-cap
questions.explanation: Multi-cap funds must invest at least 75% in equity-related instruments, with a minimum of 25% each in large, mid and small-cap stocks.

questions.text: Which of the following complaints is typically NOT handled through SCORES?
questions.explanation: SCORES addresses regulatory or procedural violations; mere dissatisfaction with performance does not qualify.

questions.text: An AIF may be set up as a trust, company, LLP or:
questions.explanation: AIFs can be established as a trust, company, limited-liability partnership or body corporate.

questions.text: Churning of client portfolios refers to:
options: Rebalancing as per agreed asset allocation
Excessive buying and selling primarily to earn higher fees or commissions
Investing in multiple funds for diversification
Switching from regular to direct plans
questions.explanation: Churning is unethical when trades are executed unnecessarily to generate more brokerage or fees, not to benefit clients.

questions.text: Advertising by SEBI-registered intermediaries must be:
options: Factually correct, fair, and not misleading
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that advertisements must be true, fair, and not misleading, and must include risk disclosures.

questions.text: The interest component of an EMI in the first few months is:
questions.explanation: Initially, outstanding principal is high; hence interest dominates early EMIs.

questions.text: A key distinguishing feature of a mutual fund compared to PMS is that:
options: Mutual funds are unregulated, while PMS is regulated
Mutual funds pool money from many investors into a common portfolio, while PMS maintains segregated portfolios for each client
Mutual funds are only for HNIs, while PMS is for small investors
Mutual funds can invest only in equity
questions.explanation: Mutual funds operate a common pool of assets, whereas PMS typically runs segregated portfolios in each client’s name.

questions.text: From an advisory perspective, why is understanding different asset classes important?
options: To match assets with client’s goals, risk profile and time horizon
To help the client avoid diversification
To recommend only one product to all clients
questions.explanation: Advisers must understand asset characteristics to recommend suitable portfolios aligned to each client’s goals and risk tolerance.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a conflict of interest?
options: Advisor’s personal or financial interest clashing with duty to client
questions.explanation: A conflict of interest arises when the advisor’s personal or financial interests may compromise objective advice to the client.

questions.text: Treynor Ratio differs from Sharpe Ratio because it uses:
options: Total risk instead of systematic risk
Systematic risk (beta) instead of total risk
questions.explanation: Treynor Ratio uses beta to measure systematic risk, while Sharpe Ratio uses standard deviation for total risk.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly ranks yield measures for a premium bond (coupon > market yield)?
questions.explanation: For a premium bond: coupon rate is highest, followed by current yield, and YTM is lowest as price will pull down to par over time.

questions.text: Modern Portfolio Theory (MPT) was first introduced by:
questions.explanation: Harry Markowitz introduced Modern Portfolio Theory in his 1952 paper 'Portfolio Selection', which mathematically demonstrated the benefits of diversification.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers must not accept funds or securities worth less than:
questions.explanation: The minimum threshold of ₹50 lakh applies to each client’s investment under PMS.

questions.text: Which of the following is a fixed expense?
questions.explanation: Rent is contractually fixed and predictable each month.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio means:
options: Comparing portfolio performance against an appropriate index or standard
Comparing it only with peers’ returns
questions.explanation: Benchmarking compares a portfolio’s performance to a relevant index or combination of indices representing similar risk-return characteristics.

questions.text: The main objective of listing securities on a recognised stock exchange is to:
options: Provide liquidity, visibility and regulatory oversight
questions.explanation: Listing enhances liquidity, visibility and investor protection through regulatory oversight.

questions.text: The first step in initiating an investment relationship with a client is:
questions.explanation: KYC compliance is the first step before any investment transaction; it verifies the client’s identity and address.

questions.text: Inspection of intermediaries by SEBI is conducted to:
options: Ensure compliance with laws and regulations
questions.explanation: SEBI inspects intermediaries to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and investor protection norms.

questions.text: Which of the following events is LEAST likely to trigger a review of a financial plan?
options: Minor fluctuation in one month’s expenses
questions.explanation: Small short-term expense fluctuations are normal; major life or financial changes warrant a plan review.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers must report performance:
options: Uniformly across disclosure documents, marketing materials, and client reports
questions.explanation: Performance must be disclosed uniformly across all communications, as per SEBI’s performance disclosure norms.

questions.text: In an EMI, the interest component:
options: Is zero in the first year
questions.explanation: As principal outstanding reduces, the interest portion of each EMI declines.

questions.text: An open-ended mutual fund scheme:
options: Allows purchase only during the NFO period
Is for a fixed term and then compulsorily redeemed
Allows continuous purchase and redemption at prevailing NAV
Cannot be bought by retail investors
questions.explanation: Open-ended schemes issue and redeem units on a continuous basis at the applicable NAV and normally operate in perpetuity.

questions.text: Which is an example of good debt?
options: Loan to buy depreciating asset on EMI
questions.explanation: Borrowing for education or business that enhances earning potential is considered good debt.

questions.text: The Certainty Equivalent Rate (CER) represents:
options: The highest return expected on a risky portfolio
The rate at which a risk-free investment is equally attractive as a risky portfolio
The average of all expected portfolio returns
The minimum guaranteed rate offered by the government
questions.explanation: CER is the rate a risk-free investment must offer to make an investor indifferent between it and a risky portfolio.

questions.text: Why is inflation an important factor in financial planning?
options: It increases the nominal value of assets automatically
It reduces the purchasing power of money over time
questions.explanation: Inflation erodes purchasing power; therefore, goals must be planned in inflation-adjusted terms.

questions.text: Recommending a highly risky product to a retired client who needs stable income is an example of:
questions.explanation: This is a breach of suitability, because the product does not match the client’s risk profile and needs.

questions.text: Perpetuity refers to:
options: Payments for a fixed number of periods
questions.explanation: A perpetuity pays indefinitely; PV = Payment / r.

questions.text: Borrowing to purchase consumables or luxury goods is generally termed:
questions.explanation: Such borrowing doesn’t create assets or future income.

questions.text: Ethically communicating risk to clients requires:
options: Highlighting only high returns in presentations
Presenting both upside potential and downside risks clearly
questions.explanation: Balanced communication should clearly explain possible losses, volatility, and risk factors along with potential returns.

questions.text: High-yield bonds are characterised by:
options: Very low default risk and low coupon
Investment-grade rating and low spread over government securities
Sub-investment grade rating and higher default risk
questions.explanation: High-yield bonds are non–investment grade and therefore carry higher default risk, compensated by higher yields.

questions.text: A person with high fixed obligations and unstable income should:
options: Reduce liabilities and build contingency reserves
questions.explanation: Such individuals should reduce leverage and strengthen liquidity.

questions.text: Bank fixed deposits (FDs) in India are insured by DICGC up to:
questions.explanation: DICGC insures bank deposits (principal plus interest) up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.

questions.text: The Capital Market Line (CML) plots:
options: Expected return against standard deviation for efficient portfolios
Expected return against beta for all securities
questions.explanation: The CML shows the relationship between expected return and total risk (standard deviation) for efficient portfolios including the risk-free asset.

questions.text: If total assets = ₹60 lakh and total liabilities = ₹25 lakh, the individual’s net worth is:
questions.explanation: Net Worth = Assets − Liabilities = 35 lakh.

questions.text: Under SEBI rules, an AMC can offer:
options: Both a value fund and a contra fund
Only a value fund but not a contra fund
Only a contra fund but not a value fund
Either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both
questions.explanation: A mutual fund house can have either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both, as per SEBI categorisation norms.

questions.case_text: Ajay, aged 45, wants to retire at 60. His current monthly expenses are ₹70,000, expected to rise by 6% annually. He expects 7% post-retirement returns and plans to live till 85. Inflation-adjusted corpus required is to be estimated.

questions.text: Highest interest rate is on:

questions.case_text: Sneha earns ₹90,000 per month, spends ₹55,000, and pays EMIs of ₹20,000. She has health insurance cover of ₹4 lakh. She wants to build an emergency fund equal to 6 months of expenses.

questions.text: Monthly surplus available:
Target emergency fund size:
Current health insurance cover:

questions.case_text: Rohit wants to buy a car costing ₹12 lakh. His bank offers a 5-year loan at 10% p.a. interest. He can pay the full price from his savings or take the loan and invest his money in a debt mutual fund earning 7% p.a.

questions.text: Loan interest rate offered is:
If Rohit takes a loan, tenure is:
Investment return from the mutual fund is:
Which option gives higher effective return?
What factor mainly decides his choice?
options: Difference between loan rate and investment return
